item.title: Lautoka next test for Suva
item.description: EXPERIENCE will be important for Suva when the side takes on Lautoka in the Subrails Marama Championship at Bidesi Park at 1pm today. The capital side has won its past three matches and will enter today’s clash with confidence after coming from behind to beat Kadavu 19-10 last Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
EXPERIENCE will be important for Suva when the side takes on Lautoka in the Subrails Marama Championship at Bidesi Park at 1pm today.

The capital side has won its past three matches and will enter today’s clash with confidence after coming from behind to beat Kadavu 19-10 last Saturday.

Kadavu led 10-7 at halftime, but Suva produced a stronger second-half performance to secure the victory and continue its push in the competition.

Captain Bulou Wainikiti Vasuturaga said the team was aware of the challenge ahead and needed to continue working on areas that required improvement.

“Every women’s team is powerful,” she said. “We just need to identify our weaknesses clearly, fix them during training, and make sure we’re better in our next game.”

The match will also provide another opportunity for Suva’s younger players to gain valuable experience alongside senior players such as Vasuturaga and Luisa Tisolo.

Head coach Meli Tuifagalele said the experience within the squad had been important in helping develop the younger members of the team.

“They came back to us at the right time. We have a very young squad,” he said.

Suva’s only defeat came against Nadi in round three, a result Tuifagalele said had highlighted the need for his players to remain disciplined and follow the structure developed during training.

The loss has since been followed by three straight victories, including wins over Kadavu and other opponents as Suva regained its momentum.

Lautoka will now provide another test for the side, with Tuifagalele expecting the Western team to adopt an expansive approach.

Suva will need to maintain its structure and make the most of its experience if it is to extend its winning run when the two sides meet today.

item.title: Tailevu ready for Kadavu
item.description: Tailevu will face a tougher test this week when it takes on Kadavu in round seven of the Skipper Cup competition. Tailevu Rugby Union president Joe Rodan was pleased with his side’s performance last week, particularly the way the players adapted to difficult weather and ground conditions.
item.content:encoded:
Tailevu will face a tougher test this week when it takes on Kadavu in round seven of the Skipper Cup competition.

Tailevu Rugby Union president Joe Rodan was pleased with his side’s performance last week, particularly the way the players adapted to difficult weather and ground conditions.

The Tailevu women’s side scored 102 points, which Rodan believes could be a record, while the other teams also secured victories to complete a clean sweep.

Rodan said the results reflected the team’s preparation and ability to perform in different conditions.

“Today I am glad to see that our boys adapted well to the weather,” he said.

“Despite the conditions we have out here in the rain and the sloppy ground, the boys adapted very well and they played according to the weather.”

He also credited the coaches, players and technical staff for their work in preparing the teams.

Rodan said the senior men’s side continued the form it showed the previous week and maintained its strong performance over 80 minutes.

The focus now shifts to Kadavu, with Rodan expecting another challenging encounter.

He said the team would need to maintain its discipline and continue building on last week’s performance as it prepares for the match.

Rodan also thanked supporters who turned up despite the poor weather conditions and urged them to continue backing the team.

He said the support would be important as Tailevu looks to raise funds and maintain its campaign in the competition.

item.title: Historic win a boom for basketball
item.description: BASKETBALL Fiji 5×5 captain Joshua Fox says the national team’s historic success in Mongolia should be a turning point for greater investment in the sport. Fiji defeated Vietnam 69-57 in their final match at the FIBA Asia Cup Pre-Qualifiers 2029, creating history and delivering one of the biggest moments for the country’s 5×5 programme.
item.content:encoded:
BASKETBALL Fiji 5×5 captain Joshua Fox says the national team’s historic success in Mongolia should be a turning point for greater investment in the sport.

Fiji defeated Vietnam 69-57 in their final match at the FIBA Asia Cup Pre-Qualifiers 2029, creating history and delivering one of the biggest moments for the country’s 5×5 programme.

While celebrating the achievement, Fox said the result also highlighted the potential of basketball in Fiji and the need for increased resources to support future development.

Fox, who first represented Fiji in 2015 in Thailand, said he had witnessed the sport’s progress firsthand.

“The first games I ever played in was in 2015, so it’s been a crazy journey to see how far we’ve come and just seeing all the steps and how much better we’ve gotten, and the younger talents that keep coming up, has been great.”

He said growing interest among local players and Fijians living overseas was another encouraging sign.

“There’s more interest from the local boys and boys from overseas as well,” he said.

“It’s always nice to see where we’ve grown without some of the funding and resources that the rest of these countries have.”

Fox said he hoped Fiji’s historic victory would encourage stakeholders to recognise the sport’s potential and provide stronger support for players and national teams.

“Hopefully now we can see that basketball can actually do something great and that we start putting resources into it,” he said.

He described the current period as pivotal for Basketball Fiji and called for increased investment at both grassroots and national levels.

“It’s a good future, but I think it’s a pivotal time for us to start actually investing in it,” he said.

Fox said he wanted more local competitions for young players, improved national team programmes, more international matches and better training camps.

With junior tournaments, including an under-15 competition expected later this year, he said the foundations were already in place for growth.

“I hope we start investing in it, doing more local competitions for all the kids in Fiji and more things for the national teams,” he said.

After making history in Mongolia, Fox said Basketball Fiji now had an opportunity to turn a landmark victory into sustained progress.

Fiji’s guard Tyrone Mclennan (with the ball) in action during their game against Mongolia in the FIBA Asia Cup 2029 Pre-Qualifiers in Mongolia last month. Picture: BASKETBALL FIJI

item.title: Final push
item.description: GLOBAL Care Suva FC’s return to the semi-finals has given the side renewed belief, but coach Pita Rabo knows the hard work must continue if they are to overcome Ba this weekend. Suva has worked through a demanding season and will now face a strong Ba side in the semi-final, with Rabo confident that the changes he made within the team are beginning to show.
item.content:encoded:
GLOBAL Care Suva FC’s return to the semi-finals has given the side renewed belief, but coach Pita Rabo knows the hard work must continue if they are to overcome Ba this weekend.

Suva has worked through a demanding season and will now face a strong Ba side in the semi-final, with Rabo confident that the changes he made within the team are beginning to show.

Rabo said the team had introduced several new aspects to its game over the past weeks, and the players were responding well to the changes.

“We put in a lot of new things in the team, and I think it’s working for us,” Rabo said.

He said the team’s preparation throughout the league and the Fiji FACT had helped build a stronger foundation as they entered the crucial stages of the competition.

“For us, it means a lot to us in terms of the way that we prepared,” he said.

However, the coach knows reaching the semi-finals is not enough, with Suva now focused on earning a place in the final.

The side comes into the match after a tough three-game stretch last week, which took its toll on some players.

“We’re straight on working with them at the moment, making sure they recover,” he said.

Despite the challenges, Rabo wants his players to remain focused and maintain the work ethic that has taken them this far.

“We just keep our heads down and keep on working hard,” he said.

He expects Ba to provide a difficult challenge and has warned his players not to underestimate their opponents.

“I expect them to go and give a tough game against Ba this week,” Rabo said.

The coach also believes Suva’s confidence and the support of its fans will be important factors when the two sides meet.

Rabo called on Suva supporters to continue believing in the team and what it can achieve.

He urged fans to travel to 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba and support the team as it battles for a place in the final.

“To all the fans out there, we’ve just been so proud that we can bring you this far,” Rabo said.

“But this is a very important week for all of our Suva fans.”

Suva will face Ba in the first semi-final match of the Extra BOG tournament this Saturday at 2pm.

item.title: Ready for the challenge
item.description: THE FIJI Water Flying Fijians have settled into preparations in Japan ahead of their Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup clash against Canada this weekend. The national side has enjoyed favourable weather and a positive atmosphere in camp, with players eager to take the field on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
THE FIJI Water Flying Fijians have settled into preparations in Japan ahead of their Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup clash against Canada this weekend.

The national side has enjoyed favourable weather and a positive atmosphere in camp, with players eager to take the field on Saturday.

Centre Tuidraki Samusamuvodre said the team had completed another training session and was looking forward to the match.

“We’ve just finished our training session here in Japan. Good weather, amazing weather and atmosphere.

“The boys are looking forward to the game this week and we look forward to it,” he said.

Samusamuvodre also called on supporters in Fiji and Japan to get behind the team.

“We need your support from Fiji and those of you here in Japan. The boys need your support here in Japan,” he said.

Assistant coach Seremaia Bai said preparations had been positive, with strong team spirit building ahead of the match.

“Good preparation and good spirit in the team.

“It’s been great to be in Japan, the weather, the lovely culture and the people and we are looking forward to this weekend.

“We thank everyone for making us feel at home,” Bai said.

The Flying Fijians will face Canada at Hanazono Rugby Stadium, with kick-off at 7pm Fiji time.

Fiji enters the match as the defending Pacific Nations Cup champion and is chasing a third consecutive title.

The Canada match is another important step in Fiji’s bid to maintain dominance in the regional competition.

item.title: Adi Fika inspires women in rugby with accreditation
item.description: ACHIEVING a World Rugby Level 3 coaching qualification is not simply a personal milestone for Adi Fika Vucago Seruitanoa. She sees it as part of a broader step forward for women in rugby.
item.content:encoded:
ACHIEVING a World Rugby Level 3 coaching qualification is not simply a personal milestone for Adi Fika Vucago Seruitanoa.

She sees it as part of a broader step forward for women in rugby.

The Get Into Rugby Plus coach and teacher at Nausori Primary School is one of only four women in Fiji to hold the World Rugby Level 3 coaching accreditation.

Originally from Deuba in Serua, with maternal links to Saqani in Cakaudrove, Seruitanoa has risen through the coaching ranks and is now head coach of the Naitasiri Women’s Senior team competing in the 2026 Subrails Marama Cup.

She is also preparing to join the Fiji Rugby Union High-Performance Unit.

However, she remains humble about her progress.

“I don’t see it as an achievement,” she said. “I see it as growth and a pathway for women in the sport of rugby.

“I was inspired by other women who went ahead of me in this arena and will continue to grow in the future.”

Her coaching journey began through the Get Into Rugby Plus programme, which she credits with opening a pathway she had never imagined.

“It was Get Into Rugby Plus that introduced me to coaching,” she said.

“The programme motivated me and gave me the passion to take up coaching, as well as changed how I become a better version of myself.”

For her, developing young players at grassroots level is crucial to Fiji’s future rugby success.

She believes strong foundations in primary schools are essential if Fiji is to produce players capable of reaching elite and international level.

“It’s always best to start small and excel from there,” she said.

Seruitanoa’s journey has not been without challenges, particularly stereotypes faced by women in a traditionally male-dominated rugby environment.

But she says she refuses to let negative perceptions stop her progress.

“The change begins with us, and the progress begins with us,” she said.

Now, after five years in the programme and steady growth in the rugby arena, she hopes more women will step into coaching and leadership roles.

“We need a lot of women in this space,” she said.

“The more we collaborate and support each other, we will close the gap between men and women in the sport.”

Her message to aspiring coaches is simple: challenges will come, but they should never become barriers — continue to grow and move forward.

item.title: Chand ends Labasa tenure
item.description: ALVIN Chand has stepped down as head coach of Extra Supermarket Labasa FC, bringing an impressive tenure with the Babasiga Lions to an end. The Labasa Football Association confirmed Chand’s resignation through its official Facebook page, citing personal reasons and ongoing work commitments.
item.content:encoded:
ALVIN Chand has stepped down as head coach of Extra Supermarket Labasa FC, bringing an impressive tenure with the Babasiga Lions to an end.

The Labasa Football Association confirmed Chand’s resignation through its official Facebook page, citing personal reasons and ongoing work commitments.

“The association would like to place on record its sincere appreciation to Alvin for his dedication, commitment and service to Labasa FC during his time as head coach,” the association stated.

“His contribution to the team and the wider Labasa football family is greatly valued, and we thank him for his efforts and professionalism.

“We respect Alvin’s decision and wish him every success and happiness in his future commitments. He will always be a valued part of the Labasa football family.”

Chand was appointed head coach in March 2025 after several years working within the district’s development system, including seven years coaching Labasa’s youth teams.

He made an immediate impact at senior level, guiding the Babasiga Lions to the 2025 BiC Fiji FACT title in his first major tournament in charge.

Labasa defeated Rewa on penalties in the final at the HFC Bank Stadium in Suva to claim its first FACT title in 10 years.

Two months later, Chand delivered another major trophy, guiding Labasa to the 2025 Extra Battle of the Giants title at Subrail Park.

The Babasiga Lions defeated Rewa 2-1 in the final in front of 7643 supporters, securing a memorable victory on home soil.

Under Chand, Labasa also reached the semi-finals of the 2025 FMF Inter-District Championship.

In the 2026 season, he guided the northern side to second place in the Extra Premier League and the semi-finals of the BiC Fiji FACT.

His final assignment came at the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba, where Labasa was attempting to defend its title.

Labasa defeated Nasinu 1-0 and Navua 2-1 but suffered a 3-0 loss to Suva. Despite winning two of its three pool matches, the Babasiga Lions missed out on a semi-final berth on goal difference.

The schoolteacher remains committed to advancing his coaching career and is close to completing his A Licence Coaching Certificate.

Meanwhile, the Labasa Football Association has appointed Solomon Islands mentor Jerry Sam as the new head coach.

Sam joined Labasa as technical adviser ahead of the 2026 Extra BOG and worked alongside Chand during the tournament.

“The association is also pleased to announce that Jerry Sam has been appointed as the new head coach of Labasa FC,” the statement said.

“We welcome Jerry into his new role and wish him all the very best as he takes on this important responsibility with the Babasiga Lions.”

item.title: Brothers live out basketball dream
item.description: three brothers from Bau Island in Tailevu with maternal links to Ono-i-Lau are living a dream that began in their backyard. For Ratu Atirieli, 24, Ratu Gabriel, 20, and 18-year-old Ratu Zechariah Tuivanuavou, Fiji’s campaign at the FIBA Asia Cup 2029 Pre-Qualifiers in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia last month became much more than an international assignment.
item.content:encoded:
three brothers from Bau Island in Tailevu with maternal links to Ono-i-Lau are living a dream that began in their backyard.

For Ratu Atirieli, 24, Ratu Gabriel, 20, and 18-year-old Ratu Zechariah Tuivanuavou, Fiji’s campaign at the FIBA Asia Cup 2029 Pre-Qualifiers in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia last month became much more than an international assignment.

For the first time, they were part of Basketball Fiji men’s 5×5 team, marking a special chapter in their family.

Ratu Gabriel previously represented Fiji in the under-23 3×3 program, while Ratu Zechariah represented Fiji during the under-17 Oceania Cup last year.

For Ratu Gabriel, playing in an international stage with his brothers is something he has dreamt about for years.

“To travel with my brothers for a tournament representing Fiji is a blessing,” he said.

“Having my brothers with me makes me feel better and enjoy the experience because I’m not far from home when I’m with them.”

Growing up, basketball was not just a game in the Tuivanuavou household. The brothers regularly competed against one another, engaging in countless one-on-one contests to settle the all-important family debate over who was the best player.

“This special moment where I could share the court with my brothers wearing the Fiji jersey is something I’ll never forget,” Ratu Gabriel said.

“It’s always been a dream to play with my brothers.”

Ratu Atirieli shares the same sense of gratitude.

“I can only give praise and thanks to God for blessing us with this opportunity,” he said.

Ratu Zechariah, who is the youngest member of the Fiji team, is among several debutants in the squad.

“Being the youngest player in the team, I’ve learned a lot from the older players, especially from their experience at high-level international tournaments,” Ratu Zechariah said.

For their parents, watching their sons in the national team was an emotional moment.

Their father said the family was overwhelmed when his sons were named in the national squad.

“We as parents got emotional when they got named to represent Fiji and it will be no different when they step on the court to play,” he said.
